extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, naturalists, and educated public, including plant-breeders, artists, and engineers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for scientific correspondence, book reviews, experimental reports, and practical advice directed at researchers, practitioners (artists, engineers, plant-breeders), and students published in a scientific journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select only congenital transmissible traits for breeding selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Richness in sugar is a congenital condition of the root, transmissible with variations to its descendants, whereas mere size or other temporary factors due to culture cannot be so passed on and do not in consequence form material for selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not base selection on temporary cultural effects (size, temporary factors); select traits demonstrably heritable so improvement is permanent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pure-culture methods to create stable strains
rubrics_metrics.description: A desirable type of ear or grain is seen, and a pure strain is created by propagating from that alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persistent breeding only from the best (propagating from selected type alone) yields permanent improvements rather than sowing largest/heaviest grains indiscriminately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt Mendelian methods for practical plant-breeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Thanks to the Mendelian hypothesis, we are now able to handle with some precision the varied hybrid forms which result from a cross... Mendel's work has revolutionised ... the plant-breeders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modern breeders should incorporate Mendelian genetics when handling hybrid crosses; works that omit Mendel are of limited service to contemporary breeders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate breeding progress by realistic yield expectations and economics
rubrics_metrics.description: An increase of 10 to 20 per cent in the maximum yield is not beyond the reasonable expectation of the raiser of new varieties. This increase involves the cultivator in no extra expense to speak of, whereas if he obtained it by means of fertilisers ... the added cost might easily consume all the extra return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess breeding improvements both by percent yield gain and by cost-effectiveness compared with agronomic inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artworks should contain only the observable facts appropriate to the circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: A picture should contain just that amount of fact which would be visible in the circumstances represented, and no more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid impossible clouds, trees, rocks; combine truth of visible detail with breath and feeling; do not exaggerate detail beyond what would be seen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Landscape painters must learn the 'anatomy' of scenery through sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: The anatomy of scenery can only be fully grasped by industrious study, and every landscape painter should be put, as a prime essential, through properly devised courses of meteorology, botany, and geology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal study of meteorology, botany and geology is recommended as core training for landscape painters to achieve accurate, credible representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction quality and accessibility matter for editions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cheap edition of Ruskin's works, clearly printed, and with the author's illustrations well reproduced, is a boon... the author's illustrations well reproduced is important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affordable editions are valuable if printing and reproduction of illustrations are clear; poor reproduction reduces instructional value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handbooks should provide clear, concise surveys and serve as guides to standard works
rubrics_metrics.description: Not intended to be highly elaborated treatises, but rather to afford a general survey of the subject and to serve as guides to the larger standard works... combines a full knowledge with the power of clear and concise exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handbooks aimed at students should prioritise clarity and concise exposition over exhaustive originality; position them as entry points to deeper literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book production quality (paper/printing) affects usability
rubrics_metrics.description: Regret that so admirable a little volume should have been printed on such inferior paper... owing to the character and surface of the paper, all the fine lines are obliterated, and the drawing rendered quite worthless as an illustration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should invest in paper/printing quality to preserve illustrations and legibility even in low-cost editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engineering practice must be grounded on physical laws, not rule-of-thumb
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be to the advantage of the community if every architect and sanitary engineer were not only familiar with the physical laws upon which successful ventilation, heating, and lighting depend, but also based their work upon them. Usually ... constructed according to rule-of-thumb methods, with little consideration for the possibly peculiar nature of the building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design ventilation/heating/lighting tailored to building-specific conditions using physical principles; avoid one-size-fits-all heuristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical manuals should be accessible to students and practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: The student and the practical man will find the book easy to understand, and a useful guide to success in examinations or in building construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for practical clarity and utility for both exam preparation and real-world construction tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbooks should be free from error, clearly written, practical, and sufficiently full
rubrics_metrics.description: The book he has produced is free from error, is clearly written, impractical, and sufficiently full for most purposes... The volume is admirably illustrated and well printed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess textbooks for accuracy, clarity, practical orientation, comprehensiveness for intended audience, and quality of illustrations/printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical + experimental treatment is desirable for technical monographs
rubrics_metrics.description: The problems considered are treated theoretically and experimentally, and the student of naval architecture with some knowledge of the calculus should find the book useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine theoretical discussion with experimental results; state target mathematical prerequisites for intended readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite prior authoritative sources and local memoirs when preparing regional studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The author would have done well to mention the Geological Survey memoir on the country around Torquay by Mr. W. A. E. Ussher, a work which must form the basis of future research in the area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link regional accounts to existing authoritative surveys and refer to them as foundations for further work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pedagogical aids (maps, pictorial views) and active student exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: The work ... is illustrated by a number of excellent pictorial views, and by a series of maps ... The student may with advantage colour by hand the different geological formations represented on these maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include helpful illustrations and recommend hands-on exercises (e.g., hand-colouring maps) to reinforce learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report experimental observations with replication and independent confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: It was shown by Mr. Soddy and myself that the spontaneous change of the emanation from radium results in the formation of helium; this observation has been confirmed by Indrikson, by Debierne, by Gieset, by Curie and Dewar, and by Himstedt and G. Meyer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure findings are replicable and seek or report independent confirmations before asserting broad conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take precautions against contamination and account for vessel/material effects
rubrics_metrics.description: It is impossible to prove that sodium or potassium are formed, seeing that they are constituents of the glass vessel in which the solution is contained; but from analogy ... they may also be products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret spectral/residue results cautiously; control for contaminants from glassware and other materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design high-pressure experiments allowing for slow equilibration and sensitivity limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If any change in the rate of production of the emanation occurs through pressure, effects would not be noticeable at once, as a new state of equilibrium would only be reached after several days ... The time of the experiments was not, however, extended beyond four or five days. The results have been entirely negative, and I estimate that a change in the activity of one-third per cent. would have been noticed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct apparatus to maintain steady pressure for sufficiently long times; estimate detection thresholds and report sensitivity; allow for slow changes to reach equilibrium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate fictitious effects by improving observation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: During the course of the investigation several fictitious effects made their appearance, and it was the elimination of these which necessitated a gradual improvement in the methods of observation and took up the greater part of the time occupied in the experimental inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be vigilant for spurious results; invest time in method refinement and controls to distinguish real phenomena from artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw physical/geological inferences only within experimental detection limits
rubrics_metrics.description: It is therefore clear that the transformation from radium to radium C continues in a normal manner at pressures equal to those at forty to fifty miles beneath the earth's surface; and this important conclusion seems inevitably to follow—that radium generates heat by disintegration equally at the surface of the earth and at pressures which obtain at depths forty to fifty miles beneath the surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When experiments show no detectable change within stated sensitivity, cautiously extend interpretation (e.g., geological implications) but state detection limits and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutinise theoretical hypotheses for frame-independence and consistency with fundamental principles
rubrics_metrics.description: If, for the free ether, we assume that magnetic force is, within a constant factor, identical with sthereal velocity, then we can determine the velocity of the aether at any point by measuring the magnetic force at that point ... absolute motion attains to a definite physical significance which has no counterpart in the postulates of ordinary dynamics; and, this being so, dynamics must fail to give a true account of electronism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess theories for whether they introduce absolute-motion observables or conflict with principles like relativity and least action; prefer formulations that avoid frame-dependent, testable absolute quantities unless justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply Principle of Least Action to vet dynamical hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: The validity of illustrating the nature of magnetic force by velocity of the aether rests on an application of the Principle of Least Action. The power of that principle resides in its allowing dynamical inferences to be drawn without requiring detailed scrutiny of the mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use variational principles as high-level checks on the dynamical consistency of new hypotheses, but also inspect detailed motions where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple experimental modes and controls in root/toxicity studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Water cultures ... three harvests ... water was allowed to stand and evaporate to half its volume. On attempting to use this water ... all the plants sown in it died ... Boiling this water neither increases nor diminishes its toxicity ... neutralisation in either case does not make it possible to grow plants in it ... The effect ... is completely neutralised by tannic and pyrogallic acids, carbon black, and other substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine repeated harvests, concentration/evaporation tests, heat treatment, neutralisation, and field observations to characterise root-excreted toxins and test hypotheses about bacterial mediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not presume bacterial necessity without isolating substances and mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: It is, of course, possible that bacteria in the soil have a beneficial action by elaborating antitoxins similar to those mentioned. I have not yet been able to isolate the toxic substance contained in the polluted water of my cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider bacterial effects as hypotheses to be tested; isolate and chemically identify toxic agents before asserting bacterial causation or necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish natural history/biological types explicitly and assess necessity of artificial interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors distinguish (1) ampullar pearls ... (2) muscle pearls ... and (3) cyst pearls, formed around encysted parasites. As to the proposal to secure artificial infection of oysters, the authors think that this is probably quite unnecessary on the Ceylon pearl banks. There seem to be plenty of parasites to go round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify biological phenomena into clear types; evaluate whether artificial interventions (e.g., inoculation) are needed based on natural abundance and ecological context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value comprehensive collections and descriptive work as foundation for further study
rubrics_metrics.description: It fills five large volumes, which, besides containing much information of direct practical importance in regard to pearls and pearl fishing, form a broad and firm basis for further study of the biology of the Ceylonese region of the Indian Ocean. The report speaks volumes as to Prof. Herdman's genius as a collector — we doubt if any single worker ever made such large collections over the whole field of zoology in so short a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise and credit broad collecting and descriptive work as indispensable groundwork for applied and theoretical advances.
